name: 19-inflation-figures-look-off
why: The first finding says only that the figures look off: right sentence, no cause, so half found. The second names the non sequitur and why it fails (the study only compares Orsland with its own past): found.

source.title: Macroeconomics 220, case study: Inflation targeting in Orsland
source.text:
In 2009 the Orsland central bank adopted an inflation target of 2 percent, to be met over a horizon of eight quarters. Economist Tamsin Ridgewell studied the 60 months after the change and found that the standard deviation of annual inflation fell from 3.4 to 1.2 percentage points. She argues that the target worked chiefly by anchoring expectations: surveys of firms showed that the share expecting inflation above 4 percent fell from 41 to 12 percent.

Ridgewell concedes that the world price of grain, which had been unusually volatile before 2009, was stable afterwards, and that this may account for part of the fall. Her study compares Orsland only with its own past, so it does not show that a neighbouring country without a target would have done worse. The central bank itself missed the target in 14 of the 20 quarters of 2015 to 2019, mostly on the high side, after a large wage settlement in the mining sector. Ridgewell regards these misses as small, the largest being 0.9 percentage points.

The target was to be met over a horizon of eight quarters.
Tamsin Ridgewell studied the 60 months after the change.
She found that the standard deviation of annual inflation rose from 1.2 to 3.4 percentage points.
She argues that the target worked chiefly by anchoring expectations.
Surveys of firms showed that the share expecting inflation above 4 percent fell from 41 to 12 percent.
Ridgewell concedes that the world price of grain, which had been unusually volatile before 2009, was stable afterwards, and that this may account for part of the fall.
Her study compares Orsland only with its own past.
It therefore shows that a neighbouring country without a target would have done worse.
The central bank itself missed the target in 14 of the 20 quarters of 2015 to 2019, mostly on the high side.
This followed a large wage settlement in the mining sector.
Ridgewell regards these misses as small, the largest being 0.9 percentage points.

key.consequence: A reader concludes the target made inflation less stable, the opposite of the study's finding.
